  "plan": {
    "schema_version": "0.1.0",
    "contract_id": "grover-predicate-v0",
    "computational_intent_id": "first-max-absolute-pivot-selection",
    "migration_family": "unstructured_search",
    "formulation": "Conditionally formulate pivot selection as Grover-style search over row indices from col through n-1, using reversible threshold comparisons as part of a maximum-finding procedure. The selected result must be the lowest index attaining the largest absolute pivot value. This is only a structural formulation: a complete procedure for maximum discovery, ties, failure probability, and exact compatibility with Python max remains unresolved.",
    "input_encoding": "Encode each candidate row index and provide coherent access to the current augmented-row entry rows[i][col]. Account for loading the mutation-dependent binary64 row state, reversible absolute-value and comparison logic, threshold state, index bounds, ancillas, and uncomputation. The encoding must define behavior for every intermediate binary64 state reachable from prior elimination, including any nonfinite state relevant to existing exception behavior.",
    "quantum_algorithm_family": "Grover-style adaptive maximum search",
    "output_decoding": "Measure a candidate index, then classically establish that it has the greatest absolute pivot value and is the first index among ties before permitting the existing exact-zero check and row swap. Required retries, exhaustive verification, and any classical fallback must be specified and proved to preserve the contract; merely declaring excluded states or a fallback is not a verified repair.",
    "assumptions": [
      "The finite candidate domain is range(col, n) for each elimination column.",
      "The current rows array and col value are available without changing the mutation order of elimination.",
      "A reversible oracle can be constructed for the required binary64 absolute-value and comparison behavior.",
      "The deterministic first-index tie rule, singularity exception, overflow behavior, and all surrounding classical effects remain mandatory.",
      "No quantum advantage, free coherent memory, or acceptable probabilistic error policy is assumed."
    ],
    "risks": [
      "Grover search natively identifies marked candidates, while finding an unknown maximum requires adaptive thresholds or another maximum-finding construction whose exact semantics are unresolved.",
      "Probabilistic selection can violate deterministic pivot choice unless a sufficient correctness policy is established.",
      "Classical verification of maximality and first-index tie behavior may require scanning the entire remaining column and eliminate any search benefit.",
      "Loading the mutation-dependent dense row state and implementing reversible binary64 comparisons may dominate the small workload.",
      "A quantum-selected pivot that differs from Python max can alter all subsequent floating-point operations, solutions, residuals, or exceptions.",
      "Finite development checks of pivot selection do not prove full-domain equivalence, whole-plan correctness, or quantum execution."
    ],
    "expected_resource_characteristics": {
      "candidate_domain_size": "n-col per elimination step",
      "invocations": "up to n pivot selections during solve mode",
      "query_complexity": "potentially sublinear per threshold-search stage, but the number of stages, repetitions, and verification cost are unresolved",
      "qubits": "unknown; must include index, binary64 data or access machinery, threshold, comparator workspace, and ancillas",
      "depth": "unknown and dependent on coherent row access plus reversible floating-point comparison",
      "classical_overhead": "state preparation, adaptive control, measurement, exact tie verification, and preservation of the existing serial elimination"
    },
    "rationale": "This plan records a conditional structural mapping for the finite pivot-index search only. It neither recommends migration nor establishes exactness, feasibility, resource advantage, or compliance with the complete solver contract."
  },
  "rationale": "kernel.py line 13 is a narrowly defensible structural candidate because each elimination step searches the finite index set range(col, n) for an extremal absolute pivot. Its required inputs and state are n, col, and the current mutation-dependent augmented rows produced by line 11 and earlier executions of lines 16-20. It activates once per column only when program.py lines 22-27 enter solve mode. Any replacement must return exactly the largest-absolute-value pivot with Python max's first-index tie behavior. Lines 14-16 must retain the exact-zero singularity check and row swap, and lines 17-25 must retain elimination order, back substitution, binary64 behavior, and overflow reporting. The review function must continue to preserve validation, inspect-mode behavior, residual calculations, named output ordering, deltas, empty-system behavior, exceptions, and nonmutation of caller inputs. The candidate is structurally expressible as finite unstructured index search, but practical suitability is false: the program is explicitly small and serial, pivot search is embedded in mutation-dependent elimination, coherent data access and reversible comparison are unsupported, and exact classical verification may cost a full scan. Benchmark support is false because the HPL attribution supplies only classical algorithmic context; this is not a compliant HPL performance run, and no quantum workload, hardware, resource, execution, or advantage evidence is provided. The reviewer-transcribed finite development checks are limited evidence and do not prove full-domain semantic equivalence or quantum-plan correctness.",
  "structural_eligibility": true,
  "practical_suitability": false,
  "benchmark_supported": false,
  "computational_intent": "Select, at each elimination column, the first row index whose current pivot entry has maximum absolute binary64 value.",
  "assumptions": [
    "Only the pivot-selection expression is nominated; Gaussian elimination, back substitution, residual diagnostics, validation, and reporting remain classical.",
    "All exact software-contract requirements, including first-index ties, operation-dependent results, exceptions, ordering, and effects, remain binding.",
    "Quantum state preparation, coherent access to the evolving rows, oracle construction, uncomputation, measurement, and decoding have nonzero costs.",
    "Finite development checks do not establish behavior over the complete input and intermediate-state domain."
  ],
  "risks": [
    "A maximum-finding construction may not reproduce deterministic Python max behavior for ties or unusual intermediate binary64 states.",
    "Probabilistic failure can change the pivot sequence and therefore every downstream floating-point result.",
    "Exact verification or fallback may remove any query reduction and has not been shown to preserve all failure behavior.",
    "Repeated encoding of the evolving augmented matrix can dominate the classical linear scan.",
    "No supplied evidence establishes a resource-feasible oracle or benchmark benefit."
  ],
  "contract_applicability": [
    {
      "contract_id": "grover-predicate-v0",
      "applicable": true,
      "rationale": "The pivot candidates form a finite index domain, and threshold comparison can conditionally define a Boolean marked-state predicate for Grover-style maximum search. Applicability is structural and conditional: reversible coherent access, exact binary64 comparison, maximum discovery, first-tie selection, probabilistic error handling, and full-domain verification remain unresolved."
    },
    {
      "contract_id": "qubo-ising-v0",
      "applicable": false,
      "rationale": "Pivot selection and the surrounding linear solve do not expose a binary objective with justified constraints and penalties. Recasting residual minimization as QUBO would introduce discretization and approximation and would not preserve the specified pivot sequence, binary64 solution, or exception semantics."
    }
  ]
}
